records.scalar: maximum number k of columns in OA(100,k,10,2), equivalently 2 plus the number of MOLS of order 10

human_baseline.author: Ernest T. Parker
human_baseline.description: A published pair of orthogonal Latin squares of order 10 gives an OA(100,4,10,2).

current_record.scope: MOLS(10) is known to have at least two and at most six squares; equivalently k=2+N(10).

records.open_evidence: This orthogonal-array cell is equivalent to T065: an OA(100,k,10,2) of index 1 corresponds to k−2 mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 10 (for k≥2). The recorded k=4 construction and 4≤k≤8 gap therefore duplicate the MOLS(10) family rather than providing an independent benchmark. Do not count T062 as a separate confirmed family. A distinct OA target with strength at least 3 or index greater than 1 still needs a public construction and an open bound gap.
checks_performed: Verified Parker’s published order-10 pair and its index-one strength-two OA interpretation.
Checked the published statement that N(10) is unknown, with interval 2 to 6 MOLS.
Translated the interval to k=4 to 8 OA columns.
Compared the OA(100,k,10,2), index-1 parameterization with the standard OA–MOLS correspondence: k columns correspond to k−2 MOLS of order 10. Identified full objective equivalence with T065.
records.remaining: Choose an OA parameter cell not equivalent to T065, preferably strength at least 3 or index greater than 1; verify a public human construction and a nonzero published bound gap before promotion.

records.scalar: maximum number of 5-subsets of a 22-set with no pair repeated, D(22,5,2)

human_baseline.author: Finite-geometry construction: projective plane of order 4, restricted to 21 of the 22 points
human_baseline.description: The 21 lines of PG(2,4) are 5-subsets with every pair occurring once; on a 22-set, leave one point unused.

current_record.value: 21 ≤ D(22,5,2) ≤ 23 by the elementary pair count
current_record.scope: A current exact-parameter specialist table was not verified; a stronger upper bound or exact result may exist.

records.open_evidence: The projective-plane construction gives 21 blocks; counting pairs gives an upper bound floor(C(22,2)/C(5,2))=23. This is a gap, but current specialist bounds and exact status were not established, so this record remains pending.
checks_performed: Replaced the solved D(19,4,2)=25 configuration.
Verified the order-4 projective plane has 21 points, 21 lines of size five, and every pair on one line.
Computed the elementary upper bound 23 by counting pairs.
Did not verify a current specialist table or rule out a stronger upper bound.
records.remaining: Find a primary packing-number table or paper for D(22,5,2), verify current endpoints, and confirm the cell is not exact.

records.scalar: maximum number N(10) of pairwise orthogonal Latin squares of order 10

human_baseline.author: Ernest T. Parker
human_baseline.description: Parker publishes a pair of orthogonal Latin squares of order 10, explicitly displayed in the paper.

current_record.scope: Pair construction is known; an upper bound of 6 follows from Bruck's theorem. Whether a triple exists remains unresolved in the cited literature.

records.open_evidence: The Waterloo-hosted primary report on MOLS states the order-10 maximum is unknown; the cited classical construction gives at least two, and Bruck's bound gives at most six.
checks_performed: Reviewed the primary MOLS reports for the explicit pair and the current interval.
Confirmed the objective is a single integer and the available interval is nontrivial; did not retype or independently verify the Latin squares.
records.remaining: Retrieve and independently check the published pair before solver benchmarking.

records.scalar: minimum size K₂(27,1) of a binary length-27 radius-one covering code

human_baseline.author: Richard W. Hamming
human_baseline.description: Puncturing four coordinates from the binary [31,26,3] Hamming code preserves radius at most one and gives a length-27 code of size 2^26.

current_record.scope: Habsieger’s improved lower bound and the punctured Hamming-code construction give a finite gap.

records.open_evidence: Habsieger proved K(27,1)≥4,793,495. Puncturing a perfect binary Hamming code gives a feasible length-27 radius-one code of size 2^26. The cited sources do not state that these bounds coincide.
checks_performed: Replaced the small length-10 radius-two candidate with length 27, radius one.
Verified Habsieger’s lower bound K(27,1)≥4,793,495.
Derived the 2^26 feasible upper bound by puncturing the [31,26,3] perfect Hamming code; puncturing preserves covering radius at most one.
Did not retrieve or replay a parity-check matrix.
records.remaining: Retrieve a public Hamming parity-check matrix and validate the punctured code’s covering radius and size.

records.scalar: maximum size of a binary length-31 code correcting one deletion

human_baseline.author: R. R. Varshamov and G. M. Tenengolts
human_baseline.description: A VT checksum class modulo n+1 gives a single-deletion-correcting code; at n=31 its classes have size 2^26.

current_record.scope: Lower endpoint is a length-31 VT class; upper endpoint is floor((2^31−2)/30) from the explicit non-asymptotic bound of Kulkarni and Kiyavash (2013). The paper identifies determining the largest single-deletion code as open and reports exact optimality only through n≤10.

records.open_evidence: The primary 2013 paper states that determining the largest single-deletion code is an open problem, reports exact optimality through lengths n≤10, and gives the general upper bound floor((2^n−2)/(n−1)) for binary codes. At n=31 this is 71,582,788, strictly above the VT construction size 67,108,864. The resulting published-source interval is nonzero.
checks_performed: Verified the primary paper calls determination of the maximum single-deletion code an open problem and gives the binary upper bound (2^n−2)/(n−1).
Evaluated the bound at n=31: floor((2^31−2)/30)=71,582,788.
Counted all 32 checksum classes of sum(i*x_i) mod 32 by exact integer dynamic programming; each class has 67,108,864 words.
Checked the later primary paper for the stated VT optimality range; n=31 is beyond proved exact cases.
records.remaining: Before solver use, retrieve a compact public VT witness description and verify the deletion-correction property with a certificate or independent checker.
